_readme: Canonical cases for skills/run-workflow/scripts/workflow.py, run by scripts/tests/workflow-runner.sh. definitions: the Build definition the tests drive, and a one-step variant. context and outputs: the start context and one passing answer per contract ({head}, {tree} and {patchId} are filled from the test's repository). catalogs: standIn is added to a copy of the real catalog (contracts are added, satisfiedBy is set); faults and sound are edited copies and the fault code each must, or must not, raise. validation: each case edits a definition (set a step's or a top-level field, drop a field, remove, move or add a step, repeat a list's first item until the list holds count items, each copy's id suffixed -2, -3 and so on, or replace it whole) and names the refusal code start must give, or ok (rehearsal true: the start says it is a rehearsal, which a gate or a checkpoint needs while it is not switched on); root says which plugin copy runs it (fixture: every step skill present; real: the plugin as released; standIn: the fixture copy with the standIn catalog); git says whether the working directory is a repository. verdicts: an answer, its contract and what its first line parses to (class null: no verdict). proofs: a proof (with the verdict value it came with, where that matters), the git answers given and whether it holds, is stale, is refused or cannot be read. repository: a remote address and the name reports carry for it. outcomes: starts are children-complete start cases (the definition's edits, the context added, and the refusal code start must give or ok); ends are Build runs answered to the end with the canned answers, a contract's verdict line replaced where answer names one, the tracker's runOutcomes (absent: the tracker named none), and the outcome finished gives, the one the step recorded and the one the last report closes the run with.

credentials._readme: Lines the credential check must catch (`caught`) and must leave alone (`kept`). Every line any earlier revision of the check caught is in `caught`, except the agreed ordinary lines in `kept`. A line that holds a provider's token prefix is a list of parts, cut inside each prefix, that the test joins, so no file holds a string a secret scanner would take for a real token.
kept: yJ is the prefix of a token
